title: Latency Photometer — field notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick, low-friction notebook to capture runs from the new 'latency-photometer' harness. The photometer is my lightweight probe for microsecond-resolution tail tracing across GPU hotpool handoff + KV cache priming. Goal is to capture patterns that the usual p99/p999 aggregates miss.

Setup summary:
- Cluster: aws-g4dn-xlarge equivalent testbed (4 vGPUs simulated via containerized runtime).
- Runtime build: branch latency-photometer (see PR above), kernel clock sampling enabled, high-res timers (chrono_ns).
- Model: distilled-opt-2b-quant (q4f) — chosen because quantized path + KV cache effects are visible.
- Workload: synthetic echo prompts, token lengths 8/64/256, arrival patterns: poisson (lambda=300 qps), and burst bursts of 2s windows at 3x lambda.
- Hotpool config: hotpool-size=8, eviction-policy=LRU, warmup-threshold=0.4 (40% GPU-util).
- Measurement: photometer hooks capture (t_enqueue, t_dispatch, t_kernel_start, t_kernel_end, t_kv_hit).

Run IDs captured:
- run-2025-01-15-a (poisson baseline, 30m)
- run-2025-01-18-b (3x bursts, 45m)
- run-2025-01-29-c (stress with preemption events, 60m)

Selected raw trace excerpt (run-2025-01-18-b) — columns: id,phase,ns_delta,kv_hit
1,enqueue->dispatch,2100,false
1,dispatch->kernel_start,4200,false
1,kernel_start->kernel_end,8600,false
2,enqueue->dispatch,1800,true
2,dispatch->kernel_start,700,true
2,kernel_start->kernel_end,4300,true
3,enqueue->dispatch,13200,false  # long enqueue in microburst window
3,dispatch->kernel_start,5400,false
3,kernel_start->kernel_end,9000,false
(IDs anonymized — sequence numbers only)

Observations / quick hypotheses:
- Microburst enqueue spikes (12ms in example above) correlate with transient queue saturation when burst arrives and hotpool refill/backoff starts.
- KV-hit requests show much lower dispatch->kernel_start latencies (~700ns in sample) — implies the runtime prioritizes hot cache paths correctly. However enqueue times still dominate overall tail.
- Kernel durations are relatively stable across hits/misses for these short prompts; variability mostly at enqueue and dispatch boundaries (scheduler/backpressure).

Early metrics (aggregated totals from photometer parser):
- poisson baseline (run-a): median end-to-end 12.8ms, p95 28ms, p99 49ms, p999 89ms
- burst run (run-b): median 13.6ms, p95 64ms, p99 210ms, p999 1.1s (long tail due to enqueue spikes)
- preempt run (run-c): median 15.2ms, p95 82ms, p99 340ms, p999 2.4s (preempt jitter + hotpool thrashing)

Quick root-cause sketch:
- When bursts hit, hotpool eviction + cold-priming of KV causes a temporary increase in enqueue queue depth. The scheduler backoffs new dispatches until a token-batch threshold is reached, causing long enqueue->dispatch windows.
- Preempt events (background maintenance) amplify effect by removing available GPU slots mid-burst, which forces additional queuing and causes p999 blow-ups.

What I tried (hacks/probes):
- Short-term mitigation: reduce warmup-threshold from 0.4 -> 0.25 in a local run: p99 improved from 210ms -> 120ms in one run, p999 still noisy.
- Probe: enabled soft-priority lanes where cached requests allowed fastpath preemption of cold-start dispatches. Result: median unchanged, but p95 dropped ~18%. Still not sufficient for p999.
- Cache priming script: I added a lightweight prefix-skimmer that issues tiny warmup requests when incoming qps rises above threshold. Reduced frequency of 12ms enqueue spikes in one test window.

Data dump snippet (CSV-style) — per-minute counts (run-b):
minute,reqs,in-queue-max,kv-hit-rate
0,18000,32,0.12
1,18240,36,0.10
2,17500,44,0.09  # start of burst window + queue climb
3,18900,68,0.11  # peak microburst
4,17000,40,0.13

Visual idea for next iteration:
- Plot two overlaid heatmaps: enqueue latency density vs time, and kv-hit-rate vs time. Expect hotspots aligned with burst windows.
- Add a stacked bar showing which phase contributed to tail (enqueue vs dispatch vs kernel).

Next actions (short list):
1) Re-run with warmup-threshold=0.2 and comprehensive telemetry (kernel preemption flags) — see ENGINF-1428. (Owner: me; timeline: this week)
2) Wire photometer traces into Console dev dashboard so we can visualize per-route heatmaps quickly. Talk to Mira for UI hooks. (infra spike; owner: Mira)
3) Prototype a small adaptive primer service: when short-term qps derivative > X, issue N warmup tokens to top-K cached prefixes. Measure cost vs tail benefit. (Owner: Riley)
4) Add a debug mode to photometer where samples include stack snapshot at long-enqueue events (to see if lock contention or syscall stall).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are enqueue spikes caused by a global lock in the local scheduler, or by per-tenant admission logic? Need a stack trace.
- Does the eviction threshold algorithm behave poorly when many small requests dominate versus fewer large ones? The synthetic workload is uniform; will repeat with mixed-length traces.
- Cost trade-off of priming: how many tokens per warmup is the sweet spot? Hard to predict without longer-run econ sims.

Notes to self (scratch):
- When reporting to SRE, include a p999-exposure window aggregated per-tenant, not just cluster-wide. Some tenants cause disproportionate tail.
- Remember to anonymize request IDs before posting any traces.
- Add a toggle to photometer to only persist traces that exceed a threshold (e.g., end->end > 200ms) to keep storage sane.

Bottom line (current):
Hotpool cold-priming + scheduler backpressure during short, high-intensity bursts is the dominant contributor to observed p999 tail. Several small mitigations (lower warmup threshold, soft-priority lanes, priming) reduce p95 but p999 requires either better admission control or fast cold-path reduction (more aggressive priming or pre-emptive allocation).

References & quick links:
- ENGINF-1428 (ticket): photometer integration and p999 analysis
- runtime PR 3142: kernel clock sampling and photometer hooks
- sketch: /confluence/eng/photometer-heatmap (placeholder)

End of note.

-- Ashish
